title: A Gravity for the Horizon
premise: Sebastian Nakamura has spent nine years alone tending Earth's last seed vault, broadcasting maintenance logs to a colony fleet that stopped answering long ago. When a distress signal arrives in a dead language, she decodes it as a warning: two rival fleets are converging on the vault's jump corridor, each believing the other destroyed it. To prevent mutual annihilation, Sebastian fabricates proof that the vault holds the genetic key both fleets need, forcing them into negotiation while concealing that the vault is nearly empty. In the end she sacrifices her anonymity and her archive to broker peace, choosing belonging among strangers over the lonely duty that defined her.
about_author: Mara Lockridge is a former agricultural scientist who spent a decade cataloguing heirloom seeds before turning to fiction. She writes quiet, character-driven science fiction about people who keep the lights on after everyone else has gone.

chapters.title: The Quiet Inventory
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. On a routine seed audit, Sebastian catalogs the vault's slow decay and records another unanswered log for the Meridian colony fleet. The emotional beat is tender loneliness: she talks to dead air as if it were family, establishing her devotion to duty and her fear that no one is left to receive it.

chapters.title: A Voice in Dead Tongues
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. A distress signal arrives in Pre-Collapse Standard, extinct for two centuries. Using her grandmother's linguistic archives, Sebastian partially decodes it: a ship claiming the jump corridor is mined. The beat is electric hope curdling into dread—someone is alive, and they are afraid of something worse than silence.

chapters.title: What the Vault Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian, with flashback interludes in her mother's voice. She searches the vault's deep storage and discovers the truth she's been avoiding: most seed stocks failed years ago; the vault is a beautiful shell. The beat is grief and shame—her logs have been a eulogy dressed as a report.

chapters.title: Two Flags on One Horizon
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian monitoring orbital traffic. Two fleets—the Meridian remnant and the Voss Expedition—drop out of jump within hours of each other, each hailing the vault with hostile demands. The beat is rising panic: her invisible sanctuary has become the flashpoint of a war neither side can afford.

chapters.title: The Lie That Holds
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Under pressure from both fleets' envoys, she broadcasts fabricated assay data proving the vault holds irreplaceable viable germplasm, proposing joint custody pending verification. The beat is vertiginous moral compromise—she lies to save lives and immediately understands the lie must grow.

chapters.title: Envoy at the Airlock
chapters.summary: POV alternating between Sebastian and Ilsa Reyes, the Meridian envoy. Ilsa arrives in person; suspicion thaws into wary intimacy as the two women work through the decryption together. The beat is fragile connection—Sebastian feels belonging stir for the first time in years, right as her deception puts it at risk.

chapters.title: Corridor of Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Investigating the original distress signal, Ilsa finds evidence the 'mined corridor' was staged by Voss hardliners—and that Sebastian's assay data doesn't match physical samples. The beat is betrayal dawning slowly; trust built across chapters begins to fracture under one discrepancy.

chapters.title: Ninety-Six Hours
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. With the jump window closing and both fleets arming, Sebastian confesses everything to Ilsa: the empty vault, the forged data, the decades of unanswered logs. The beat is raw catharsis—she surrenders the lie and asks Ilsa to help her build something true before the window shuts forever.

chapters.title: The Weight of Seeds
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian during the climax. She broadcasts the full truth to both fleets alongside a genuine offering: the vault's surviving heritage collection and Earth's restoration protocols, arguing that survival means nothing without something to survive for. Fleets hold fire as the window narrows; the beat is desperate, defiant hope.

chapters.title: A Gravity for the Horizon
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian, months later. The fleets have formed a provisional council; the vault becomes shared ground, its remaining seeds divided and planted aboard ships. Sebastian, no longer caretaker but citizen, records one final log—not to dead air, but to companions. The beat is quiet resolution: belonging found not by keeping the past alive, but by giving it away.
